COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS 
ABA No.1006 of 2023 
Hon’ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
 Mr. Aditya Singh, learned counsel for the 
applicant. 
2. Mr. G.S. Sandhu, learned G.A. through V.C. with 
Mr. K.S. Rawal, learned AGA for the State. 
3. Heard. 
4. Applicant is before this Court seeking 
anticipatory bail in connection with FIR No.0032 dated 
11.03.2017 which was registered at P.S. Pant Nagar, 
District Udham Singh Nagar, for the offences u/s 420, 
465, 466, 468, 471, 474, 120-B, 34 IPC and Sections 
8/9 of the Prevention of Corruption Act (S.T. No.4 of 
2020, State v. Balwant Singh and others pending 
before the Court of Sessions/Special Judge, P.C. Act, 
Nainital). 
5. It is the contention of learned counsel for the 
applicant that the said FIR was lodged against as many 
as 113 accused persons in respect of same land scam, 
which is commonly known as ‘N.H. Ghotala in 
Uttarakhand’. It is further submitted by him that most 
of the accused persons have been enlarged on bail by 
this Court, and many of them have been given 
anticipatory bail by this Court. He further submitted 
that this is a case of parity. 
6. Per contra, learned State counsel does not 
dispute this fact of the case being of parity with those 
who have already been released on bail or anticipatory 
bail. Some orders passed by this Court are also 
annexed by the applicant as Annexure No.7 in the 
paper book of this anticipatory bail application.  2
7. In the facts and circumstances of the case, the 
applicant- Prabhsharan Singh is directed to be released 
on Anticipatory Bail, in the event of his arrest, on 
executing a personal bond of Rs.30,000/- and 
furnishing two reliable sureties, each in the like 
amount to the satisfaction of the SHO concerned, on 
the following conditions:- 
(i) Applicant shall attend the court proceedings 
regularly and will not seek any unnecessary 
adjournment; 
(ii) Applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any 
inducement, threat or promise to any person 
acquainted with the facts of this case. 
(iii) Applicant shall not leave the country without the 
previous permission of this Court. 
8. The anticipatory bail application stands disposed 
of accordingly. 
(Pankaj Purohit, J.) 
 14.12.2023 R.Dang

COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
ABA No.1006 of 2023
Hon’ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
Mr. Aditya Singh, learned counsel for applicant. 
2. Mr. S.C. Dumka, learned AGA for the State.
3. Heard.
4. Applicant was involved in connection with FIR 
No.0032 dated 11.03.2017 which was registered at P.S. Pant 
Nagar, District Udham Singh Nagar, for the offences u/s 
420, 465, 466, 468, 471, 474, 120-B, 34 IPC and Sections 
8/9 of the Prevention of Corruption Act. He moved ABA 
No.1006 of 2023 which was disposed of by reason of 
judgment dated 14.12.2023 with certain conditions, one of 
which was Condition No.(iii) which provided that he shall 
not leave the country without the previous permission of this 
Court. 
5. Applicant has now moved the application (MCRC 1 
of 2024) in the said anticipatory bail application requesting 
to relax the aforesaid condition and to permit him to visit 
USA for a period of two months. The application is 
supported by affidavit. It is stated in paragraph no.5 of 
application that applicant is a Green Card Holder of USA 
and in order to retain the said status, he is required to travel 
once in 180 days to the said country to maintain his status;
and he is an Indian Passport Holder bearing No.M7135700 
issued by Regional Passport Office, Dehradun having 
validity till 01.03.2025. 
6. Pursuant to the time given by this Court, the State has 
filed its objection to the said application wherein it is mainly  2
stated that his presence is required in the criminal 
prosecution launched against him, as referred hereinabove. 
7. I have considered the rival submissions of parties and 
perused the record as well. In order to procure the 
attendance of applicant in this criminal prosecution, as 
referred above, this Court felt it necessary that the applicant 
should submit details of his property before this Court and 
an undertaking should be filed that he would not alienate or 
dispose of his property during his absence from India and 
that he would report to this Court once he returns back.
8. Pursuant to the aforesaid directions, applicant filed 
supplementary affidavit before this Court on 21.05.2024, 
along with which, copy of Khatauni of his property of Fasli 
Year 1398-1403 was filed; today on 05.06.2024, an 
undertaking is also furnished before this Court by the 
applicant, copy whereof has duly been served upon the 
respondent –State. 
9. In such view of matter, Misc. Application (MCRC/1/ 
2024) is allowed. Condition No.(iii) imposed vide order 
dated 14.12.2023 is relaxed to the extent that the applicant is 
permitted to visit United States of America for a period of 
two months commencing from the date of his departure 
which according to learned counsel for applicant is in the 
month of July, 2024, subject to purchase and availability of 
air tickets. He shall immediately report his arrival in India 
to this Court. 
(Pankaj Purohit, J.)
 05.06.2024 R.Dang

Hon’ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
Mr. Aditya Singh, learned counsel for 
the applicant.
2. Mr. Bhaskar Chandra Joshi, learned 
A.G.A. with Mr. Vipul Painuli, learned Brief 
Holder for the State of Uttarakhand.
3. The applicant has moved miscellaneous 
application No.4 of 2024 for permitting him 
to travel United States of America for a 
period of two months or any such further 
order as this Hon’ble Court may deem fit 
and proper.
4. The respondent-State was given 
opportunity twice to file objection to the said 
application, but, it has not filed any 
objection so far, therefore, this Court has no 
option but to proceed for disposal of the 
aforementioned application, which is 
pending since long.
5. Applicant was involved in connection 
with FIR No.0032 dated 11.03.2017 which 
was registered at P.S. Pant Nagar, District 
Udham Singh Nagar, for the offences u/s 
420, 465, 466, 468, 471, 474, 120-B, 34 
IPC and Sections 8/9 of the Prevention of 
Corruption Act. He moved ABA No.1006 of 
2023, which was disposed of by reason of 
judgment dated 14.12.2023 with certain 
conditions, one of which was Condition 
No.(iii) which provided that he shall not 
leave the country without the previous 
permission of this Court.
6. Applicant has moved miscellaneous  2
application (MCRC/1/2024) for permitting 
him to visit USA for a period of two months. 
Said application was granted by this Court 
by a reason of order dated 05.06.2024 and 
he was allowed visiting USA for a period of 
two months commenced from his date of 
departure. However, it was also directed
that he shall immediately report his arrival 
to this Court. The applicant departed to USA 
pursuant to the order dated 05.06.2024 on 
02.07.2024 and returned to India on 
28.07.2024, as it is reflected from annexure 
No.1 to the earlier application 
(MCRC/3/2024).
7. The applicant in the present application 
made the same prayer. Since, the applicant 
has obeyed this Court’s order and returned 
to India and intimated about his arrival to 
the Court by filing an application 
(MCRC/3/2024), this Court has no reason to
deny permission to applicant to visit USA for 
a period of two months as prayed by him.
8. Accordingly, miscellaneous application 
(IA/4/2024) is allowed. Condition No.(iii) 
imposed vide order dated 14.12.2023 is 
relaxed to the extent that the applicant is 
permitted to visit United States of America 
for a period of two months commencing 
from the date of his departure which 
according to learned counsel for applicant, is 
in the month of March, 2025, subject to 
purchase and availability of air tickets. He 
shall immediately report his arrival in India 
to this Court. 
 (Pankaj Purohit, J.)
 27.02.2025
PN

ABA No.1006 of 2023
Hon’ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
Mr. Aditya Singh and Mr. Amanjot 
Singh Chadha, learned counsel for the 
applicant.
2. Mr. S.C. Dumka, learned A.G.A. with 
Ms. Sweta Badola Dobhal, learned Brief 
Holder for the State of Uttarakhand.
3. Applicant was involved in connection 
with FIR No.0032 dated 11.03.2017 
which was registered at P.S. Pant Nagar, 
District Udham Singh Nagar, for the 
offences u/s 420, 465, 466, 468, 471, 
474, 120-B, 34 IPC and Sections 8/9 of 
the Prevention of Corruption Act. He 
moved ABA No.1006 of 2023, which was 
disposed of by reason of judgment and 
order dated 14.12.2023 with certain 
conditions, one of which was Condition 
No.(iii) which provided that he shall not 
leave the country without the previous 
permission of this Court.
4. Applicant has now moved 
miscellaneous application No.6 of 2025
for permitting him to travel United States 
of America for a period of one month. It 
is stated in Para 6 of the said application 
that applicant is a Green Card Holder of 
USA and in order to retain the said 
status, he is required to travel to the said 
Country once in 180 days and he is an 
Indian Passport Holder bearing  2
No.C3444285 issued by Regional 
Passport Office, Dehradun having validity 
till 08.10.2034.
5. Pursuant to the time given by this 
Court, State has filed its objection along 
with delay condonation application. Delay 
in filing the objection is condoned. 
Objection is taken on record. Delay 
Condonation Application (IA/7/2025) 
made therefor, is allowed.
6. Learned State Counsel objected the 
misc. application for giving permission to 
the applicant to visit USA only on the 
ground that his visit is affecting the trial. 
7. Applicant was earlier allowed to visit
USA for a period of two months 
commenced from his date of departure
vide this Court’s order dated 27.02.2025. 
However, it was also directed that he 
shall immediately report his arrival to this 
Court. The applicant departed to USA 
pursuant to the order dated 27.02.2025
on 25.03.2025 and returned to India on 
19.05.2025, as it is reflected from 
annexure No.A.5 to the Misc. Application.
8. Since, the applicant has obeyed this 
Court’s order and returned to India and 
intimated about his arrival to the Court 
by filing an application (IA/5/2025), this 
Court has no reason to deny permission 
to applicant to visit USA for a period of 
one month as prayed by him. Further, 
the objection raised by learned State 
Counsel is misconceived. The appearance 
of the applicant-accused is required only  3
at the time of recording of statement 
under Section 313 Cr.P.C. Therefore, this 
Court is of the view that by merely 
allowing the application of the applicant 
for permitting him to travel USA is not 
coming in the way of proper proceedings 
of the trial.
9. Accordingly, miscellaneous 
application (IA/6/2025) is allowed. The
applicant is permitted to visit United 
States of America for a period of one 
month commencing from the date of his 
departure, subject to purchase and 
availability of air tickets. He shall 
immediately report his arrival in India to 
this Court. 
 (Pankaj Purohit, J.)
 07.10.2025

2. Mr. Saurabh Bhardwaj, learned Brief 
Holder for State of Uttarakhand/respondent.
3. Applicant was involved in connection with 
FIR No.0032 dated 11.03.2017 which was 
registered at P.S. Pant Nagar, District Udham 
Singh Nagar, for the offences u/s 420, 465, 
466, 468, 471, 474, 120-B, 34 IPC and 
Sections 8/9 of the Prevention of Corruption 
Act. He moved ABA No.1006 of 2023, which 
was disposed of by reason of judgment and 
order dated 14.12.2023 with certain 
conditions, one of which was Condition No.(iii) 
which provided that he shall not leave the 
country without the previous permission of this 
Court.
4. Applicant has moved miscellaneous 
application No.10 of 2026 for permitting him 
to travel United States of America for a period 
of two months. It is stated in Para 6 of the 
said application that applicant is a Green Card 
Holder of USA and in order to retain the said 
status, he is required to travel to the said 
Country once in 180 days and he is an Indian 
Passport Holder bearing No.C3444285 issued  2
by Regional Passport Office, Dehradun having 
validity till 08.10.2034.
5. There is no objection from the side of 
learned State Counsel.
6. Applicant was earlier allowed to visit USA 
for a period of one month commenced from 
his date of departure vide this Court’s order 
dated 07.10.2025. However, it was also 
directed that he shall immediately report his 
arrival to this Court. The applicant departed to 
USA pursuant to the order dated 07.10.2025
on 05.11.2025 and returned to India on 
02.12.2025, as it is reflected from annexure 
No.A.4 to the Misc. Application.
7. Since, the applicant has obeyed this 
Court’s order and returned to India and 
intimated about his arrival to the Court by 
filing an application (IA/8/2026), this Court 
has no reason to deny permission to applicant 
to visit USA for a period of two months as 
prayed by him. 
8. Accordingly, miscellaneous application 
(IA/10/2026) is allowed. The applicant is 
permitted to visit United States of America for 
a period of two months commencing from the 
date of his departure, subject to purchase and 
availability of air tickets. He shall immediately 
report his arrival in India to this Court. 
 (Pankaj Purohit, J.)
